judged_text: Guest deduplication compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email) even though email addresses are case-insensitive and no lowercasing is applied to the submitted guest. Submitting 'John@X.com' when 'john@x.com' is already an attendee passes the filter and creates a second attendee row differing only in case — the guest receives duplicate emails and appears twice on the calendar and in the ICS invite.

Submitting 'John@X.com' when 'john@x.com' is already an attendee passes the filter and creates a second attendee row differing only in case — the guest receives duplicate emails and appears twice on the calendar and in the ICS invite.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduplication uses a case-sensitive comparison (`guest === attendee.email`) and does not normalize either side (no `toLowerCase()` on `guests` or existing `attendee.email`). This allows adding the same address with different casing (e.g., `John@X.com` vs `john@x.com`), creating duplicate attendee rows and triggering duplicate downstream effects (calendar/ICS + emails). The UI-side Zod refine in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` also uses raw strings/`Set`, so it won’t catch case-variants either.
